chunks: And with this chain of narrators, from Ali ibn Abdullah, who said: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

about Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He: 'Did He have knowledge of location before He created location? Or did His knowledge come when He created it or after He had created it?' So he (peace be upon him) replied: 'Exalted is Allah! Rather, He was always knowing of location before its formation, just as His knowledge of it after He formed it. And likewise His knowledge of all things is like His knowledge of location.' The compiler of this book, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'A proof that Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, is Knowing is that actions, differing in estimation, opposite in planning, and unequal in craftsmanship, do not occur in the manner of wisdom from one who does not know it, nor do they continue on an organized path from one who is ignorant of it. Do you not see that one who does not know goldsmithing cannot craft an earring, governing its work and placing each of its fine and coarse parts in its place? Nor can one who does not know writing compose a book in which every letter follows the one before it? And the Knowing One is more subtle in craftsmanship and more brilliant in arrangement than what we have described. Therefore, its occurrence from one who is not Knowing of its manner before its existence is more distant and more impossible. And the confirmation of this is:'
ai.seo_question: Did Allah learn about space when He created it, or was He always aware of it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid affirms the eternity of Allah's knowledge (‘ilm al-dhati) by using space (al-makan) as a primary example, demonstrating that His awareness of created attributes precedes their existence. Shaykh al-Saduq reinforces this through an analogical argument (qiyas), asserting that the intricate order of the universe could not originate from ignorance, thereby proving the necessity of a Knower who possesses complete foreknowledge of His craft.
